title: Whitney's characterisation of $2$-connected graphs
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on a vertex set of at least three vertices. Then the vertex connectivity satisfies $\kappa(G) \ge 2$ if and only if for every pair of distinct vertices $u, v$ there exist two internally disjoint $u$--$v$ paths, that is, two paths from $u$ to $v$ whose only common vertices are the endpoints $u$ and $v$.
hypotheses_covered: conclusion is an iff: $\kappa(G) \ge 2$ versus existence of two internally disjoint paths between every distinct pair
